title: Trace sampling and cost experiment notes - week of 2026-05-12
content:
Purpose:
Quick capture of the sampling experiments and the associated dash/alert changes we ran this week. Goal: reduce tracing ingestion cost by ~40% without losing signal for P99 latency and error root cause analysis for customer-facing routes.

Summary (high level):
- Ran staggered sampling experiments across three route classes: public-api (high QPS), background-workers (batch jobs), and model-inference-hot (dedicated low-latency routes).
- Initial outcome: ~38% reduction in span storage and trace ingest (estimate) with visible improvement in cost telemetry.
- Discovered a blind spot: errors from model-inference-hot were under-sampled when we used uniform probabilistic sampling; switched to adaptive error-preserving sampling mid-week.

What we changed (implementation notes):
- sampling policy rollout (see OBS-412):
  * public-api: reduced uniform trace sampling from 20% -> 8% for successful requests; kept all errors and high-latency traces (latency threshold = 800ms).
  * background-workers: changed from 100% to reservoir sampling with target retention 5% for normal jobs; always keep traces for job failures and retries > 2.
  * model-inference-hot: started at 30% uniform, observed drop in coverage for error types -> switched to adaptive sampling using rule: keep 100% traces with error or with model token length > 1024 or latency > 500ms; probability floor 10% for everything else.
- Added a lightweight preprocessing step in the trace-lambda to tag candidate traces with routing_class and model_token_estimate (cheap token estimate to avoid full decode).

Standup/drilldown log (daily):
- Mon 2026-05-11: kickoff, Priya and I validated sampling lib changes in staging. Diego started dashboard for per-route trace-rate and per-token storage. TODO: add a synthetic traffic job to simulate long prompt lengths.
- Tue 2026-05-12: initial small-canary on 10% of production traffic for 'public-api' and 'background-workers'. Observed 12% reduction in trace-ingest immediately on canary nodes. Noted that our existing dashboards had no per-model-token axis — created provisional panels.
- Wed 2026-05-13: mid-week kitchen-sink incident (high latency for payments-route). Because errors were retained, tracing allowed quick RCA: a retry storm from payment-gateway B. Key win: sampling change did not obscure this path. Switched model-inference-hot to adaptive sampling after finding missing rare error spans.
- Thu 2026-05-14: full rollout to remaining production clusters for background-workers and public-api. Dashboard shows trace ingest drop ~38% from baseline (baseline = avg over Apr-May). Ran cost estimation calc (see "Cost impact" section).
- Fri 2026-05-15: post-rollout, validation queries and a small user feedback pass from support team. Next steps / follow-ups scheduled.

Dashboards and alerts updated this week: (names in Redwood Console)
- Observability / Ingest / Trace-rate-by-route (new panel) — shows sampled trace rate and estimated unsampled equivalent.
- Observability / Cost / Trace-storage-by-model (new panel) — token-attributed storage estimate using token_estimate tag.
- Alerts: trace-ingest-drop-warning (to avoid accidental over-sampling) and trace-error-preservation (fires if error retention drops below 99%).

Cost impact (rough estimate):
- Baseline avg daily span ingests (May run rate): ~1.2M spans/day.
- Post-rollout estimated span ingests: ~740k spans/day. ~38% reduction.
- Rough monthly storage saving at current vendor pricing: $11k -> $6.8k (savings ~ $4.2k/month). These are quick estimates; finance review pending before quoting to leadership.

Key decisions and rationale:
- Decision: adopt hybrid sampling (probabilistic baseline + deterministic rules for errors/long traces) for 90% of routes. Rationale: keeps tail fidelity while reducing bulk.
- Decision: keep background-job traces at reservoir target 5% because the signal-to-noise ratio for successful runs is low and we can reconstruct via metrics.
- Decision: instrument a cheap token estimator at edge to allow per-model storage attribution without heavy compute.

Open questions / risks:
- Are we missing any mission-critical internal routes that need 100% trace retention (e.g., audit/logging pipelines)? Action: Diego to inventory by 2026-05-20 (OBS-412 subtask).
- Accuracy of token_estimate: currently ~±10% for most requests. Risk: under-attribution might mislead billing or cost-optimization. Action: Noelle to run sample-based calibration job (GitHub PR referenced).
- Vendor ingestion quotas: aggressive sampling changes could mask sudden telemetry outages. Mitigation: new alert trace-ingest-drop-warning added.

Action items (owner - due):
- Priya: finalize and merge sampling lib PR and add feature flags (PR 278) - due 2026-05-18.
- Diego: complete dashboard cleanup and add comparison to last-90d baseline - due 2026-05-19.
- Noelle: run token_estimate calibration suite and publish a short note w/ error bars - due 2026-05-20.
- Liam (me): write up a short 'what changed' summary for CS & SRE and post to #obs-announce - due 2026-05-14 (done).

Notes-to-self / loose thoughts: 
- Consider an experimental 'burst-capture' mode: temporarily raise sampling to 100% for a small window when downstream alerts spike to enable richer RCA (toggleable in console). Could reduce mean time-to-detect but we need quota controls.
- Longer-term: move sampling logic into envoy filter so we can decide pre-ingest in the API edge rather than trace-lambda. Tradeoffs: complexity vs. earlier signal.

References + related tickets:
- OBS-412 (sampling rollout plan)
- OBS-387 (dashboard: per-token attribution)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/278 (sampling middleware + feature flag)

Quick retrospective (what worked / what didn't):
- Worked: rule-based retention for errors preserved RCA capability (big win).
- Worked: lightweight token estimator gave enough signal for cost dashboards without heavy compute.
- Didn't work: uniform sampling for model-inference-hot lost rare error spans — we adapted mid-week but should have test scenarios for long prompts.

Next sync items for Monday 2026-05-18:
- Priya demo merging flow and feature-flag toggles + rollout playbook.
- Diego shows dashboard baseline comparisons and per-model cost attribution.
- Noelle reports calibration results and next steps for token estimator.

(End of notes)

- aggregations: sum(span_size_bytes) GROUP BY model_tag, day
